A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original sampling and aggregation experiments, component ablations, trajectory analyses, and appendix evaluations on harder benchmarks and variable-length reasoning.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds larger-backbone evaluations, MATH500 results, and measured inference latency.

M1.justification: The MC-dropout and AGN sampling procedures, LatentRM architecture and contrastive objective, and aggregation algorithms remain unchanged, including Appendices D and H. Latent-SFT and RoT are additional evaluation backbones; no new procedural adaptation is specified.

E1.justification: v4 Table 1 adds MATH500 evaluation with RoT-2B and RoT-4B. GSM8K-Test, GSM8K-Hard, MultiArith, GPQA, and AIME were already evaluated in v2 and remain, making this a limited expansion of mathematical-reasoning data coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained sampling, aggregation, ablation, and explicit-reasoning comparisons. The new backbone tests reuse deterministic decoding as the control, and the latency comparison reuses explicit CoT. Latent-SFT and RoT serve as backbones for the proposed sampling framework.

E3.justification: v4 substantially expands evaluated configurations with Latent-SFT and Qwen3-VL-based RoT at 2B and 4B, using a 64-thought cap and coverage at N=8 and 16. Appendix F.2 adds latency measurement at N=1 and 32 on one H100. Section 5.3 also changes the reported dropout rate from 2 to 0.2; v2 Appendix G already specified 0.2, so this correction does not establish rerunning.

E4.justification: New Appendix F.2 separates sampling and aggregation latency to examine whether scoring overhead undermines latent reasoning's efficiency. Existing component ablations, diversity sensitivity, trajectory visualizations, and variable-length analysis are retained; the latter moves from F.2 to F.3.

E5.justification: Figures 2 and 6 report means over three runs in both versions. v4 introduces no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure; its added tables do not specify additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial results for Latent-SFT and RoT plus actual runtime measurements. Table 1 reports RoT-4B MATH500 deterministic/Cov@8/Cov@16 values of 0.203/0.218/0.220. Table 4 reports N=32 totals of 1.708 seconds for COCONUT and 9.802 for CoT, including 0.386 seconds of COCONUT aggregation. These are newly reported experiments. Existing results remain, with 28.924 to 28.9 in the ablation table being equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, sampling and loss equations, Bayesian and Taylor-expansion reasoning in Appendix B, and cumulative-scoring derivation in Appendix C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: enabling parallel latent TTS through stochastic sampling and contrastively trained LatentRM aggregation. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations about generalization to larger backbones, using fixed backbone-specific perturbation ranges without per-dataset tuning, and sampling dominating aggregation latency because latent trajectories are short. Existing exploration-mechanism explanations, aggregation failure explanations, and harder-benchmark limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 adds deployment guidance: GPT-2-style dropout rates of 0.1–0.3 and noise scales of 0.5–0.7, versus 0.01–0.03 for both on Llama-style models. v4 also documents new backbone configurations and single-H100 timing hardware. These disclosures supplement the unchanged LatentRM training recipe and code-access information.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations for Latent-SFT's vocabulary-space-superposition work and Render-of-Thought to accompany their evaluation. The related-work discussion in Section 2 and positioning against soft thinking in Appendix A remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 expands setup and deployment prose, inserts Section 6.2 and Appendix F.2, updates subsection references, and adds acknowledgments and a conference-status header. Most existing prose remains verbatim. The new latency paragraph contains an unresolved 'Table ??' reference.

P2.justification: v4 adds the backbone-results and latency tables, relocates and reformats existing tables, and enlarges Figure 5 with color-matched caption text. Existing plotted data and figure panels are retained, and the overall two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: Table 1 broadens empirical support for sampling generalization, while Table 4 adds practical latency evidence beyond v2's decoding-step comparison. The deployment guidance also improves usability. These are useful but bounded gains: the new backbone results measure coverage rather than LatentRM-selected accuracy, and the latency experiment leaves its dataset and sample count unspecified. The core method and principal aggregation evidence remain unchanged.
